title: Open3DFlow: An Open-Source EDA Platform for 3D Chip Design with AI Enhancement
problem: The absence of specialized electronic design automation (EDA) tools and standardized design flows for 3D chiplets remains a critical barrier to scalable 3D IC design.
motivation: To provide an open-source EDA platform for 3D IC design that integrates multi-physics analysis and enables AI-enhanced design automation.
method: The tool runs a seven-step design workflow for 3D chips that simulates the physics of vertically stacked silicon: thermal behavior, signal integrity (electrical signal propagation), and through-silicon vias (the tiny holes connecting layers). Language models automate bonding pad placement and script generation for the design tools, and the platform enables face-to-face layer coupling using a custom bonding approach, as demonstrated on a 3D RISC-V CPU with stacked memory built in the GF180 manufacturing process.
key_novelty: The platform is an open-source tool for designing 3D stacked chips that combines language model automation for design decisions with complete physics simulation to verify the design works.
contributions: Comprehensive 7-step 3D IC design workflow with TSV, thermal, and SI modeling
Implementation demonstrating 3D RISC-V CPU with stacked L2 cache in GF180
LLM-enabled automation for bonding pad placement and script generation
Open-source framework enabling AI integration and cross-domain design co-optimization
limitations: The platform compatibility with commercial PDKs requires specific manual handling; scalability on advanced technology nodes remains to be demonstrated.
